newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo up to new peak on results, upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo up to new peak on results, upgrades.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc resumed their advance on Tuesday, bolstered by a wave of broker upgrades after posting strong results last week, dealers said.
The shares got an additional boost after the UK drug giant said that Sweden had given it approval to market Naramig, a treatment for migraines, dealers said.
By 0948 GMT the shares were up 40p, or 3.6 percent, to 1157-1/2, having climbed as high as 1165 earlier.
Glaxo said Sweden was the first country to grant regulatory approval for the drug and would act as the reference member under the European Commission's mutual recognition procedures.
Both DLJ and Smith Barney upgraded Glaxo on Monday to "outperform" from "underperform."

The company last week posted an 18 percent increase in 1996 pre-tax profits. Glaxo said its profits could be flat during the next two years after its blockbuster Zantac loses its U.S. patent in July, but would then return to double-digit growth in 1999. --Scott McCormack, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366
